limitations: Coallocation reduces warm caller allocation count from5 to4; max_align_t padding can increase requested bytes (8 observed on Windows). Cold bootstrap/replacement allocation/copy paths remain separate, and a replaced embedded first-route tail stays in the parent block until result destruction.

Parent Future/token/cancel watch, native Future/wire/reply, route payload copies, gates, heap/timer and physical duties remain real costs. This is not zero-overhead. Caller-owned retained result storage leaves client quotas at publication.

Same-function unpinned serial closed-loop benchmark covers affinity0/1 and pipeline1/32 with identical public API/peer/flags/common objects. Only client/route objects swap. Caller-observed FIFO completion includes admission/queue/validation/head-of-line; first-window costs remain. Global heap/backing runs include peer mechanical tails.

Native client/pool/cache/Core sources and layouts are unchanged. That is compatibility evidence, not a new native-I/O performance measurement. Footprint single combines XRT/product; static/shared primary rows are product-only, adjacent core artifacts are inventoried separately.
